questions.prompt: Solubility of a salt is 40 g per 100 g water at 50 °C and 20 g at 10 °C. A saturated solution in 200 g of water is cooled from 50 °C to 10 °C. What mass of crystals forms?
questions.explain: Per 100 g: 40 − 20 = 20 g. For 200 g of water: 40 g.

questions.prompt: Which test could show that a sample is a suspension and not a colloid?

questions.prompt: A chef says that heating a sugar syrup lets them dissolve more sugar, but it can crystallise when it cools. Explain using the idea of solubility.
questions.modelAnswer: The solubility of sugar increases with temperature, so hot water can dissolve more sugar before becoming saturated. When the syrup cools, the solubility falls, so the solution holds more sugar than it can at the lower temperature. The extra sugar comes out of solution as crystals (crystallisation).
rubric: On cooling, solubility falls below the amount dissolved
